knowledge_point.title: Writing First-Order Linear ODEs in Standard Form

question.:question/problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
3 \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} - 4 \cos{(x )}=- 2 y \sin{(x )} + 4\,.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x).
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{gathered}3 \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} - 4 \cos{(x )}=- 2 y \sin{(x )} + 4 \\ 3 \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + 2 y \sin{(x )}=4 \cos{(x )} + 4 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(\frac{2 \sin{(x )}}{3})}_{P(x)}y=\underbrace{\frac{4 \cos{(x )}}{3} + \frac{4}{3}}_{Q(x)}\end{gathered}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=\frac{2 \sin{(x )}}{3}$ and $Q(x)=\frac{4 \cos{(x )}}{3} + \frac{4}{3}.$

question.:question/problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{8 x - 2 y}{x}\,.
$$

Assume $x\ne 0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x).
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{gathered}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{8 x - 2 y}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{8 x}{x}-\frac{2 y}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + \frac{2 y}{x}=\frac{8 x}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(\frac{2}{x})}_{P(x)}y=\underbrace{8}_{Q(x)}\end{gathered}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=\frac{2}{x}$ and $Q(x)=8.$

question.:question/problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} \cos{(3 x )} - 2 y \sin{(3 x )} + 8 \sin{(6 x )}=0\,.
$$

Assume $\cos{(3 x )}\ne 0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x).
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{gathered}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} \cos{(3 x )} - 2 y \sin{(3 x )} + 8 \sin{(6 x )}=0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} \cos{(3 x )} - 2 y \sin{(3 x )}=- 8 \sin{(6 x )} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} - \frac{2 y \sin{(3 x )}}{\cos{(3 x )}}=- \frac{8 \sin{(6 x )}}{\cos{(3 x )}} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} - 2 y \tan{(3 x )}=\frac{- 16 \sin{(3 x )}\cos{(3 x )}}{\cos{(3 x )}} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(- 2 \tan{(3 x )})}_{P(x)}y=\underbrace{- 16 \sin{(3 x )}}_{Q(x)}\end{gathered}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=- 2 \tan{(3 x )}$ and $Q(x)=- 16 \sin{(3 x )}.$

question.:question/problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} \cos{(x )} + y \sin{(x )} + \sin{(2 x )}=0\,.
$$

Assume $\cos{(x )}\ne 0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x).
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{gathered}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} \cos{(x )} + y \sin{(x )} + \sin{(2 x )}=0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} \cos{(x )} + y \sin{(x )}=- \sin{(2 x )} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + \frac{y \sin{(x )}}{\cos{(x )}}=- \frac{\sin{(2 x )}}{\cos{(x )}} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + y \tan{(x )}=\frac{- 2 \sin{(x )}\cos{(x )}}{\cos{(x )}} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(\tan{(x )})}_{P(x)}y=\underbrace{- 2 \sin{(x )}}_{Q(x)}\end{gathered}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=\tan{(x )}$ and $Q(x)=- 2 \sin{(x )}.$

question.:question/problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} y + 8 x^{2} y=2 x y^{2}\,.
$$

Assume $y\ne 0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first-order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x)\,,
$$

Converting the given equation to standard form, we have

$$
\begin{gathered}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} y + 8 x^{2} y=2 x y^{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} y + 8 x^{2} y - 2 x y^{2}=0 \\ y (\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + 8 x^{2} - 2 x y)=0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} + 8 x^{2} - 2 x y=0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+\underbrace{(- 2 x)}_{P(x)}y=\underbrace{- 8 x^{2}}_{Q(x)} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} - 2 x y=- 8 x^{2}\end{gathered}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=- 2 x$ and $Q(x)=- 8 x^{2}.$

$$
\left(\frac{1}{x^{2}}\right)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{8 x + 2 y}{x}\,.
$$

Assume $x\ne 0$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
A first order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x)\,,
$$

where $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ do not depend on $y.$
